subject: Onboarding: cost & performance tuning — agenda and owners
messages:
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Kickoff request — Redwood onboarding & cost/perf tuning

Hi Vivek,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Acme is excited to move to a short onboarding pilot. Before we lock in dates Procurement asked that we share a concrete implementation plan that focuses on cost/performance tradeoffs. Top-line targets: ~200 requests/sec steady, p95 generation latency under 300ms for most prompts, and keep production token cost under our internal goal.

Key concerns from engineering: how quantization will impact output quality for our instruction prompts, where we should place caching to maximize hit rate given our prompt variability, and the routing policy for burst capacity (we may want regional fallback). Could you put together an agenda and proposed owners for batching, caching, quant profiles, and routing tests? We can then route that to Procurement so they can approve dates.

Also attaching a small sample of prompts and a slice of token distribution for context (will send shortly). Proposed kickoff window: Tue Dec 7 or Wed Dec 8, morning PST.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
Head of AI Product, Acme Corp
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T09:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff request — Redwood onboarding & cost/perf tuning

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear targets. Attaching a focused agenda and a short workload summary to make the kickoff productive (attachments: onboarding-cost-perf-agenda.pdf, customer_workload_summary.csv). Proposed 60-minute kickoff: Tue Dec 7 10:00–11:00 PST. Calendar invite link: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=dec07-10am-pst-onboard. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2026-0847.

Agenda (high level):
- 10m: Objectives & success criteria (Acme) — confirm p95/p50 latency and cost targets
- 15m: Baseline & data — workload distribution, token mix, sample prompts (we need ~500 prompt examples)
- 15m: Cost/perf levers and quick wins:
  - batching: target batch sizing, dynamic vs fixed policies
  - caching: prefix vs KV cache placement, expected hit-rate assumptions
  - quantization profiles: int8/int4 options, accuracy guardrails and test plan
  - routing policies: primary region, burst routing, fallback to cheaper variants
- 15m: Roles, mutual action plan, milestones and SOW/DocuSign timeline
- 5m: Q&A and next steps

Proposed owners from Redwood (can adjust):
- Mutual action plan & customer liaison: Monica Patel (CS)
- Baseline performance & quant profiles: Rishi Malhotra (Applied ML / Inference)
- Integration point & batching/caching instrumentation: Laura Bennett (Solutions)
- Product constraints & roadmap alignment: Marissa Cole (Product)

Action before kickoff: please upload ~500 sample prompts (diverse categories) and a short list of production SLOs you care about. If Procurement needs SOW language before the meeting we can provide a short draft.

I'll attach the agenda now. If Dec 7 10:00 PST works I'll send the formal invite.

Thanks,
Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T11:15:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Kickoff request — Redwood onboarding & cost/perf tuning (mutual action plan draft)

Team — copied Sarah so Acme sees the draft MAP items before kickoff. Quick proposed split and incremental milestones we can review on Tue: 

Mutual action plan (draft):
1) Baseline capture (owner: Rishi) — run synthetic and sample-prompt profiling by 2026-12-10; deliver baseline report (latency distribution, token mix, KV cache opportunities).
2) Batching + instrumentation (owner: Laura) — implement SDK-level batching prototypes and telemetry hooks by 2026-12-14; deliver expected batch size recommendations and latency impact numbers.
3) Quantization profiles (owner: Rishi + Marissa) — evaluate int8/int4 profiles on a held-out eval set by 2026-12-20; include quality diffs and fallback thresholds.
4) Routing & fallback tests (owner: Vivek + Laura) — define policy for burst routing and regional fallback; run simulated failure test by 2026-12-22.
5) Procurement & SOW (owner: Vivek) — provide SOW draft and rough pricing bands to Procurement by 2026-12-09 so they can review with legal.

Immediate asks for Acme before kickoff: sample prompts (~500), representative traffic logs (anonymized), and any forbidden output/guardrails. Sarah — can you confirm when those will be available so Rishi can begin the baseline?

I'll prepare a short onboarding checklist to circulate after the meeting (networking requirements, API keys, KMS notes, and observability endpoints).

- Monica
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-12-06T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff request — Redwood onboarding & cost/perf tuning

Thanks — Dec 7 10:00 PST works for us. I've uploaded a small sample of prompts and a token slice to the Drive folder you linked and attached the file here (acme_sample_prompts.jsonl). Procurement is looped for the SOW timeline; they'll review the SOW draft when you send it.

A few clarifications ahead of the kickoff:
- Our main production workload is mixed: customer support prompts (~60%), product-search prompts (~30%), and short-form generation (~10%).
- We care a lot about semantic fidelity on instruction prompts — please include a quota for human review if quality drops beyond a threshold.
- Preferred quant profile: if there is a low-quality hit on int4 for the instruction set, plan to failover to int8 for that model ID.

See you Tue.

Cheers,
Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
Head of AI Product, Acme Corp
Attachment: acme_sample_prompts.jsonl (3.2KB)
